manifest.name: Project Mail Plugin
manifest.description: Turn emails received in your mailbox into tasks and log their content as internal notes.
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

behavioral_notes.observation: The core inbox-to-task endpoint the add-in calls. It browse()+exists()-validates both partner_id (returns {'error': 'partner_not_found'}) and project_id (returns {'error': 'project_not_found'}), defaults a missing subject to _('Task for %s', partner.name), then creates a project.task with_company(partner.company_id) using name=email_subject (raw subject, NOT html2plaintext'd unlike crm_mail_plugin's lead path), partner_id, description=email_body (raw email content), project_id, and user_ids=[Command.link(request.env.uid)] so the API-key user is assigned as the task owner. Returns {'task_id': record.id, 'name': record.name}. No stage is set, so project.task create defaults (project's first kanban stage, etc.) apply downstream.

The project lookup/typeahead endpoint backing the sidebar project picker. Searches project.project by name ilike search_term (default limit=5) and returns a list of {project_id, name, partner_name (project.partner_id.name), company_id} per hit. It iterates projects.sudo() to read those fields, so the picker can surface projects the searching user might not otherwise have field-read rights on; the access gate happens earlier in _get_contact_data (project.task create access), not in this search itself.

On-the-fly project creation from the add-in when no target project exists yet. It does request.env['project.project'].create({'name': name}) with no sudo and no extra defaults (no partner, no company override), returning {'project_id': record.id, 'name': record.name}. Standard project.project create defaults (company, default stages, privacy) apply. Exposure of the 'create project' option is gated upstream via can_create_project = project.project.has_access('create') set in _get_contact_data.

This module does NOT enrich partners; it extends the parent mail_plugin._get_contact_data to append a 'tasks' key (and 'can_create_project' flag) to the sidebar contact card. The whole 'tasks' branch is skipped unless project.task.has_access('create') is True, so the Project section disappears for users who cannot create tasks (graceful degradation, as if project were not installed). For a known partner it searches project.task by partner_id (limit 5), then filters to tasks whose project the user can read via partner_tasks.project_id._filtered_access('read').ids, returning {task_id, name, project_name} only for accessible projects. It also overrides _mail_content_logging_models_whitelist (adds 'project.task') and _translation_modules_whitelist (adds 'project_mail_plugin'), both behind the same task-create access check.

All three jsonrpc routes use the custom 'outlook' auth method inherited from mail_plugin (not defined here). It reads the HTTP Authorization header, strips a leading 'Bearer ' prefix, and validates the token via res.users.apikeys._check_credentials(scope='odoo.plugin.outlook', key=access_token); on success it request.update_env(user=user_id) to take the API-key user's identity and update_context. Missing/invalid tokens raise werkzeug BadRequest. The token itself is minted by mail_plugin's auth flow (HMAC auth code -> short-lived apikey); the bearer plumbing lives entirely in the parent module.

No OWL/JS: 0 js_files, no registry adds, no patches, no services. The 2 xml_templates are the to_translate translation bundles (translations_gmail.xml, translations_outlook.xml) shipped for the external add-in UI, not Odoo client assets. The only backend view data is views/project_task_views.xml, an ir.actions.act_window (project_task_action_form_edit) used by the plugin to redirect the user to the newly created project.task form in edit mode. The actual sidebar UI lives in the Outlook/Gmail add-in client (external to Odoo); this module is purely a route+ORM backend.

it_architecture.application: project_mail_plugin (mail-plugin Project backend; auto-installed bridge between project and mail_plugin)
logical_data_erm: project.task -> res.partner (partner_id, supplied by parent mail_plugin lookup)
project.task -> res.users (user_ids, the outlook API-key user)
project.project -> res.partner (partner_id, surfaced in search results)
information_flows: depends: project, mail_plugin (inherits outlook auth, IAP enrich, partner lookup)
inbound: Outlook/Gmail add-in -> Bearer token (Authorization header) -> _auth_method_outlook -> res.users.apikeys validation -> identity switch
side-effect: /mail_plugin/task/create -> project.task.create (name from email subject, description from email body, partner_id, project_id, user_ids=current user) -> project default stage applies
read-flow: /mail_plugin/project/search -> project.project search (ilike) -> sudo()-read picker rows for the sidebar
read-flow: _get_contact_data override -> project.task search by partner_id -> _filtered_access('read') project filter -> tasks surfaced in sidebar contact card
upstream dependency: mail_plugin.res_partner_get resolves/enriches the partner before this module attaches its task list / creates a task

capabilities: Capture a Project Task from an Inbox Email
Search/Lookup Projects from the Mail Sidebar
Create a Project On-the-fly from the Inbox
Surface a Contact's Existing Tasks in the Mail Sidebar
Log Email Content onto a Task (internal note)
value_streams: Inbox-to-Task: read email -> resolve sender as partner (parent) -> pick or create a project -> one-click create project.task with subject+body, self-assigned -> hand off to Project delivery
Contact context loop: open an email -> see that contact's existing tasks (name/project) without leaving the mailbox
policies: Capability gating: the 'tasks' section, task creation, content logging and translation whitelist are exposed only when project.task.has_access('create') is True
Project-create option gated by project.project.has_access('create') (can_create_project flag)
Sidebar task list filtered to projects the user can read via project_id._filtered_access('read')
outlook bearer-token policy: res.users.apikeys scope odoo.plugin.outlook validated per request (plumbing inherited from mail_plugin)
stakeholders: Project member / Internal User (reads inbox, creates tasks)

classification.apqc_category: 5.0 Deliver Services (service request intake / 5.x project.task engagement)
classification.rationale: project_mail_plugin is a thin service-intake extension of Project (a value-shop): it captures inbound work requests from the mailbox and turns an email into a project.task at the very front of the deliver-services value-shop loop (diagnose -> plan -> execute -> control). The core activity is creating a project.task (subject->name, sender->partner_id, body->description, project_id, self-assigned) and surfacing a contact's existing tasks in the inbox, i.e. work-request intake feeding the Project delivery engine. It inherits Project's shop classification and is a primary activity. The APQC map (apqc_odoo_map.tsv) anchors project.task to 5.x Deliver Services / shop; this module is the inbox-to-task intake at that category's front edge. It is a feeder/bridge (auto_install) onto project.task/project.project, not its own value stream, but the work it performs is engagement intake, hence 'shop'/'primary' rather than 'support'.

standard_capabilities: one-click task creation from an email (subject->name, body->description, sender->partner_id, chosen project_id, self-assigned)
project name typeahead/search returning {project_id, name, partner_name, company_id}
on-the-fly project creation from the add-in
show a contact's existing tasks (name, project) in the add-in contact card, filtered to readable projects
log email content as an internal note on a project.task
access-gated Project section that hides when the user cannot create tasks
typical_fits: services/project teams triaging shared or personal mailboxes who want inbox-to-task capture
standard project.task defaulting (first kanban stage, company, privacy) on plugin-created tasks
Outlook and Gmail add-ins reusing the shared mail_plugin auth/enrich plumbing
self-assignment of the created task to the acting user via user_ids Command.link
common_gaps: no stage/deadline/tag/priority assignment on plugin-created tasks (project defaults only)
subject is stored raw (no html2plaintext) so HTML-ish subjects pass through unsanitized; body description is the raw email content
project_create takes only a name (no partner/company/template), so on-the-fly projects start bare
task list capped at 5 by partner with no pagination; no opportunity/sale linkage stamped by the plugin path
drive_hints: odoo shell: p = env['res.partner'].search([('email','!=',False)], limit=1); pr = env['project.project'].search([], limit=1); t = env['project.task'].with_company(p.company_id).create({'name':'Inbox subject','partner_id':p.id,'description':'email body','project_id':pr.id,'user_ids':[(4, env.uid)]}); (t.id, t.stage_id.name, t.project_id.name)
odoo shell: env['project.project'].search([('name','ilike','a')], limit=5).mapped(lambda r: (r.id, r.name, r.partner_id.name, r.company_id.id))

open_questions: Exact project.task defaults (stage_id/company_id/privacy) for a plugin-created task with no stage context beyond with_company.
Whether email_body/description is sanitized for HTML anywhere downstream (none applied in this module, and subject is not html2plaintext'd unlike the crm lead path).
Whether any add-in client uses project_create to spin up bare projects in production, or only targets existing ones via project/search.
